title: Bijectivity of the explicitly constructed completed tensor map
statement: Let R and S be commutative rings, S an R-algebra finite as an R-module, R Noetherian, and p a prime ideal of R. The explicitly constructed S-algebra map AdicCompletion.completionFiniteExtensionTensorMap R S p [new-completion-finite-extension-tensor-map] is bijective.

proof.text: Set A=R_p, m=pA, C=AdicCompletion m A, B=A tensor_R S, J=pB. Localization preserves Noetherianity and base change preserves module finiteness, so A is Noetherian and B is finite over A.

Apply the finite-module completion tensor theorem to B over A. If necessary first replace the finite A-module B by a linearly equivalent module in the universe of A. This gives bijectivity of C tensor_A B → the m-adic module completion of B.

Tensor associativity and cancellation identify C tensor_A (A tensor_R S) with C tensor_R S. Since J=mB, extension of ideal powers identifies the submodule m^n B with the underlying A-submodule of J^n for every n. The identity of B induces compatible quotient bijections and hence a bijection of inverse limits from the module completion to AdicCompletion J B. On c tensor s the composite has nth coordinate equal to the image of c_n times the image of 1 tensor s; these are precisely the coordinates of the explicitly constructed map. Pure tensors additively generate, so equality on them proves equality of the maps. Bijectivity follows.
